title: Judge Not
summary: Jesus turns again to the multitude and teaches them not to judge, saying that the measure and judgment they use will be measured to them.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus turns again to the multitude and speaks to them.
Jesus teaches that they should not judge, and that the judgment and measure they use will be returned to them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus is visibly addressing the gathered multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific setting and the multitude's appearance are not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Judge not, that ye be not judged.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The teaching is spoken instruction, not a separate visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict judgment as a literal supernatural event.

title: The Mote and the Beam
summary: Jesus uses the comparison of a mote in a brother’s eye and a beam in one’s own eye to teach that a person should correct their own fault before helping a brother.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus asks why a person notices the mote in a brother’s eye but not the beam in their own eye.
Jesus says the person should first cast the beam out of their own eye, then see clearly to cast the mote out of their brother’s eye.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues speaking to the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: The mote and beam are figures in a teaching; their literal appearance is not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Thou hypocrite, first cast the beam out of thine own eye;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The mote and beam are metaphors; do not depict them as physical objects in eyes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a literal eye-injury scene or invent a brother as a present character.

title: Holy Things and Pearls
summary: Jesus teaches the multitude not to give holy things to dogs or cast pearls before swine, warning of trampling and harm.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus tells his listeners not to give that which is holy unto the dogs or cast pearls before swine, warning that they may trample them and turn to rend them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues the sermon to the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether the animals are shown is not specified; the warning may be conveyed as teaching.

spoken_dialogue.text: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage presents a warning within Jesus’s teaching.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a literal confrontation with animals or identify specific recipients.

title: Ask, Seek, Knock
summary: Jesus teaches that those who ask receive, those who seek find, and those who knock will have the door opened to them.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus teaches his listeners to ask, seek, and knock, and says these actions will receive, find, and be answered with an opening.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues speaking to the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: No asker, seeker, door, or response is specifically staged as a present event.

spoken_dialogue.text: Ask, and it shall be given unto you;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The sayings are instruction, not a narrated scene of a door opening.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible divine figure or a particular answer to a request.

title: A Father’s Gifts
summary: Jesus asks whether a father would give his son a stone instead of bread or a serpent instead of a fish, then teaches that the Father in heaven gives good things to those who ask.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus asks whether a man would give his son a stone when asked for bread, or a serpent when asked for a fish.
Jesus says that even evil people know how to give good gifts to their children, and that the Father in heaven gives good things to those who ask him.

unspecified_visual_details: The father, son, bread, stone, fish, and serpent are examples in the teaching, not identified as present people or objects.

spoken_dialogue.text: who, if his son ask bread, will give him a stone?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: how much more shall your Father who is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The father-and-son examples are rhetorical teaching.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Father in heaven or turn the examples into a separate event.

title: Do Unto Others
summary: Jesus teaches the multitude to do to others what they would have others do to them.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus teaches that people should do to others what they would want others to do to them, calling it the law and the prophets.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues speaking to the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: No example of people treating one another is supplied.

spoken_dialogue.text: do ye even so to them,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a teaching, not a depicted interpersonal event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a particular act of kindness or conflict.

title: The Strait Gate
summary: Jesus contrasts a wide gate and broad way leading to destruction with a strait gate and narrow way leading to life, and says few find the latter.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus teaches that the wide gate and broad way lead to destruction and many enter there.
Jesus teaches that the strait gate and narrow way lead to life and few find them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues his teaching to the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: The gates and ways are figures in a teaching; their literal design and any travelers are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Enter ye in at the strait gate;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: strait is the gate, and narrow is the way,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The contrast is a teaching, not a narrated journey.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict destruction or life as visible destinations or invent travelers.

title: Known by Their Fruits
summary: Jesus warns of false prophets in sheep’s clothing and teaches that they are known by their fruits, using trees and fruit as comparison; trees without good fruit are hewn down and cast into the fire.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus warns of false prophets who come in sheep’s clothing but are inwardly ravening wolves.
Jesus says people will know them by their fruits and asks whether grapes are gathered from thorns or figs from thistles.
Jesus contrasts good trees bringing forth good fruit with corrupt trees bringing forth evil fruit.
Jesus says every tree that does not bring forth good fruit is hewn down and cast into the fire, and repeats that people will know them by their fruits.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues his sermon to the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: The false-prophet imagery and tree imagery are teaching figures; their literal visual realization is not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Wherefore, by their fruits ye shall know them.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The imagery of wolves, fruit, and trees is figurative teaching; no literal transformation or tree-cutting event is narrated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a false prophet’s inward nature as a literal transformation.

title: Doing the Father’s Will
summary: Jesus teaches that not everyone who calls him Lord will enter the kingdom of heaven, reports what many will say in that day, and declares that he will tell those workers of iniquity to depart from him.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus teaches that entry into the kingdom of heaven is for the one who does the will of his Father in heaven, not everyone who says Lord, Lord.
Jesus says many will claim they prophesied, cast out devils, and did wonderful works in his name.
Jesus says he will declare that he never knew them and command workers of iniquity to depart from him.

unspecified_visual_details: The future speakers and the day mentioned are not shown as present; no heavenly setting is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: I never knew you; depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The reported claims and future declaration remain part of Jesus’s teaching; do not stage them as a current event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show prophesying, casting out devils, wonderful works, or a judgment scene as occurring now.

title: The House Founded on Rock
summary: Jesus likens one who hears and does his sayings to a wise man who builds a house upon rock; rain, floods, and winds beat upon it, but it does not fall.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus likens one who hears and does his sayings to a wise man who built a house upon rock.
Rain, floods, and winds beat upon the house, but it does not fall because it was founded upon rock.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues teaching the multitude; the house comparison may be represented as illustrative imagery.
unspecified_visual_details: The wise man’s appearance, the house’s design, and the landscape are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: whoso heareth these sayings of mine and doeth them,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew,

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent occupants, damage, or additional weather effects.

title: The House Founded on Sand
summary: Jesus likens one who hears but does not do his sayings to a foolish man who builds a house upon sand; rain, floods, and winds beat upon it, and it falls greatly.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus likens one who hears but does not do his sayings to a foolish man who built a house upon sand.
Rain, floods, and winds beat upon the house, and it falls, with a great fall.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues teaching the multitude; the house comparison may be represented as illustrative imagery.
unspecified_visual_details: The foolish man’s appearance, the house’s design, and the landscape are not specified.
